 STL’s normalised net profit zooms 8,800% on-year to ₹356 crore in Q2FY27, reports highest-ever revenue
 STL had reported a PAT of ₹4 crore in the corresponding quarter a year ago. Its net profit stood at ₹197 crore in Q1FY27. EBITDA surged by 500% year-on-year to ₹846 crore, including a one-time net gain of US tariff refund worth ₹161 crore.

 Image for representation only. NEW DELHI: Homegrown optical fibre cable (OFC) maker Sterlite Technologies (STL) on Friday reported an 8,800% year-on-year surge in normalised profit after tax (PAT) to ₹356 crore on revenue of ₹2,529 crore in Q2FY27.
“STL also reported a net debt-free balance sheet this quarter, with PAT at ₹517 crore (and a normalised PAT of ₹356 crore), driven by strong revenue growth and margin expansion,” the Pune-based indigenous vendor said.
 STL had reported a PAT of ₹4 crore in the corresponding quarter a year ago. Its net profit stood at ₹197 crore in Q1FY27, representing an 80.7% sequential growth on a normalised basis. EBITDA surged by 500% year-on-year to ₹846 crore, including a one-time net gain of US tariff refund worth ₹161 crore.
 Advt 
 The company said it reported its “highest-ever revenue”, which increased by 145% year-on-year in the July to September quarter of FY27. It attributed the revenue growth to multiple factors, including the demand for AI-ready digital infrastructure as hyperscalers build out data centers that require denser fibre per rack versus earlier architectures.
 “A growing share of the business now comes from integrated optical connectivity solutions, with the optical connectivity attach rate reaching an all-time high of 24% during H1 FY27,” STL said, adding that large multi-year agreements with hyperscalers and telecom operators supported strong order intake and steady execution through the quarter.
 Its open order book stood at ₹35,274 crore at the end of the September quarter.
 In the first half of the fiscal year 2027, it won a $1.2 billion multi-year long-term agreement with a hyperscaler to supply optical connectivity products from CY26 to CY30; a $1.11 billion deal with a hyperscaler to supply optical connectivity products from FY27 to FY29; a $288 million deal with a hyperscaler for high-density optical fibre cable products from CY27 to CY29; a $210 million deal for a leading telecom infrastructure company for high-density optical fibre cables from CY27 to CY29; and a multi-year optical cable supply agreement worth ₹960 crore with a leading Indian telecom operator.
 Advt 
 “Q2 FY’27 is our best quarter yet, with the highest revenue and EBITDA in STL’s history. It reflects the strength of demand for AI-ready digital infrastructure,” said Ankit Agarwal, MD, STL, in the earnings statement. “The large multi-year agreements we secured this quarter, along with an open order book of ₹35,274 crore, give us strong visibility as hyperscalers and telecom operators scale their digital infrastructure and networks,” he added.
 STL's stock closed 3.43% higher at ₹829 on the BSE Friday.
